acceptance_criteria.criterion: All three grid creation sites pass a valid grid ID and GridStorageInterface to DataGrid::create()
A shared JsonFileStorage instance exists and is reused
All three pages render correctly (manual verification)
No PHP errors or warnings on page load

summary: Added Manager::getGridStorage() static method to Manager.php — lazily creates a shared JsonFileStorage pointing to APP_ROOT/storage/grid-settings
PHPStan passes in webcomics-builder (0 errors after clearing cache)

comments.note: Manager.php uses a static property (self::$gridStorage) for lazy initialization of the shared JsonFileStorage. The APP_ROOT constant is referenced at runtime; if the constant doesn't exist at the time getGridStorage() is first called, it would throw an error. This is safe given the current bootstrap.php flow, but worth noting as a coupling.

The webcomics-builder references mistralys/application-datagrids via dev-main from GitHub. The vendor folder must be manually synced or composer update run when application-datagrids changes locally. A path repository entry in composer.json (repositories: [{type: path, url: ../tools/application-datagrids}]) would eliminate this manual step.

summary: AC1: ComicBookmarksPage, DetailedListPage, and EpisodeListPage all call DataGrid::create(id, Manager::getGridStorage()) with unique grid IDs.
AC2: Manager::getGridStorage() implements a lazy static singleton (éprivate static ?JsonFileStorage $gridStorageé) — shared instance confirmed.
AC3: ComicBookmarksPage grid ID is 'comic-bookmarks' (line 160 of ComicBookmarksPage.php).

AC4+5: PHPStan reports 0 errors on all 144 analyzed files. PHP -l syntax check passes on all 4 modified files. 98 webcomics-builder tests pass (1 skipped, pre-existing). Vendor copy of DataGrid in webcomics-builder has the correct mandatory signature.

comments.note: Manager::getGridStorage() references APP_ROOT constant at runtime. If called before bootstrap (e.g., in a CLI context), it would fail. Safe in current request lifecycle, but the coupling is worth noting.

JsonFileStorage::set() uses file_put_contents() which returns false on write failure without throwing an exception. If storage/grid-settings has incorrect permissions, writes would silently fail. A guard with error_log or exception would improve diagnosability.

summary: Code review PASS. Manager::getGridStorage() is a clean lazy-singleton factory returning GridStorageInterface — correct abstraction level, consistent with existing Manager static method patterns. All three Page files use \Manager::getGridStorage() with unique kebab-case IDs: comic-bookmarks, comic-list, episode-list. Fully-qualified calls are correct PHP for global-namespace classes referenced from namespaced code. JsonFileStorage path (APP_ROOT/storage/grid-settings) is constant-based — not user-controlled input, no injection risk. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: Manager::getGridStorage() correctly declares its return type as GridStorageInterface rather than the concrete JsonFileStorage. This is the right abstraction level — all three call sites depend on the interface, making future storage backend changes transparent to callers.

The \Manager:: fully-qualified call prefix in all three Page files is correct PHP. Page classes are in the WebcomicsBuilder namespace (or sub-namespace) and Manager lives in the global namespace. Without the leading backslash, PHP would incorrectly search the local namespace first. The Developer applied this consistently across all three files.

Minor style gap: in Manager.php, there is no blank line between the closing brace of getGridStorage() and the opening of addSuccessMessage(). The rest of the Manager class uses blank lines between methods. Non-blocking cosmetic issue.
